text:
alex.s: escalating ACME production issue — SSE streams get truncated when routed through their gRPC->HTTP1 intermediary. Client sees partial events and then reconnects; sometimes duplicates. Customer says this started after their gateway upgrade yesterday. Repro attached below.

jess.support: thanks — can you paste request-id + region? quick symptom: truncation only via their gateway or all clients? :eyes:

alex.s: request-id: rwd-req-9a3f, region: us-west-2. Only repros when traffic goes through their envoy-like gateway that translates http2 -> http/1.1. Direct calls to our hosted endpoint stream fine.

alex.s: minimal curl repro (they used a long-lived SSE client):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate?model=rw-infer-1" --http2 --no-buffer
```

alex.s: from customer logs (gateway):
```
[2026-03-15T14:12:03.123Z] upstream_write failed: broken pipe
[2026-03-15T14:12:03.124Z] http/1.1 response completed, size=512
[2026-03-15T14:12:03.125Z] client reconnect after 2.1s, last-event-id present
```

rohit.sre: sounds like chunk boundary coalescing or early FIN on the upstream socket. Common when h2->h1 translators merge small DATA frames into a single chunk and then the receiving proxy sends a final chunk without preserving SSE event boundaries. Do we see any `transfer-encoding: chunked` vs `content-length` toggles in our logs?

alex.s: our edge logs show `transfer-encoding: chunked` preserved, but the gateway logs show `Content-Length: 512` on the downstream response. might be their gateway adding a content-length after buffering.

maria.eng: if the intermediary buffers until it decides a content-length can be calculated, then it will buffer the stream and emit a non-chunked response => client sees truncated stream (only buffered part) then connection close. For SSE we must keep chunked and flush per event. Can we detect this and add a keep-alive newline to force flush?

rohit.sre: temporary debugging steps:
- ask customer to enable passthrough/no-buffer mode on their gateway (envoy `streaming` or `proxy_buffering off`).
- enable our `x-redwood-proxy-debug: 1` header on requests so we can correlate server vs gateway flushes.

ops-liz: FYI I spotted `x-rl-remaining: 0` on one of the traces — could be rate-limiter closing streams aggressively when quota runs out. Not sure if that's the same trace as rwd-req-9a3f though.

alex.s: good catch. customer says they saw 429s a minute earlier but denied any throttling at the gateway. Attaching full trace with headers:
```
-> GET /v1/streams/generate
host: api.redwood.ai
authorization: Bearer <redacted>
accept: text/event-stream
user-agent: acme-sse/1.2

<- HTTP/1.1 200 OK
transfer-encoding: chunked
x-rl-remaining: 0
x-request-id: rwd-req-9a3f
```

jess.support: next step: can you collect a pcap or HTTP dump between their gateway and our edge? if they can't, ask them to reproduce with `--no-buffer` curl and paste the raw bytes.

alex.s: customer provided a tiny Python repro using `requests` + `sseclient` that reproduces in ~30s when routed through the gateway. Pasting steps:
1) run SSE server request via our endpoint
2) gateway translates to http/1.1 and buffers for 512 bytes
3) gateway sends a final chunk and closes -> client reconnects

maria.eng: I think we should make the runtime emit an explicit `\n\n` separator after every SSE event so intermediaries that buffer still see a clear flush candidate. It's a mitigation, not a fix. I'll open a PR for a small change to ensure event flushes end with two newlines and `flush()` on the socket path.

rohit.sre: also check that our runtime doesn't set `Content-Length` on streaming endpoints when proxies upstream set it incorrectly. We only send chunked, but our internal edge sometimes rewrites for small initial payloads.

ops-liz: on the billing/throttle angle — if `x-rl-remaining: 0` then the request might be flagged and closed by an automated policy in the gateway. That would explain abrupt closes even if we still have open tokens. I'll ask infra to check rate-limit service logs for rwd-req-9a3f.

deploy-bot: hotfix branch `runtime/sse-flush-mitigate-177950` created by maria.eng — CI queued.

jess.support: thanks. Action items:
- alex.s: collect HTTP dump (client <-> gateway <-> our edge) + full header sets and drop in the ticket.
- rohit.sre: confirm whether edge ever rewrites chunked -> content-length for streaming.
- maria.eng: PR and short-term mitigation patch.
- ops-liz: check rate-limit logs and correlate.

alex.s: will get the dump from the customer and upload here. I also asked them to toggle `streaming` mode on their gateway; they said they can test in a staging route tomorrow morning PST.

rohit.sre: if customer can't change gateway config, we may need to add a server-side compatibility mode that inserts extra flush/newline. Let's wait for the dump but keep the mitigations ready.

jess.support: noted. keep updates here. :spiral_note_pad:
